research_question: Does canonical -10s remain a reasonable reference on matched LOW/HIGH support; are -20/-30 consistently better, how does 0 compare, and does non-causal +10 warrant a separate timing audit?
target_contract: Reuse LOW<=outer-train Q(1/3), HIGH>=Q(2/3); exclude strict middle; fit once per target/fold on full canonical train complete cases, unchanged across lags
timestamp_convention: Record-relative 10s window bounds, not wall-clock PM emission timestamps; negative means EEG earlier; gap-aware exact lookup, no previous-available substitution
preprocessing: Unchanged canonical float32 371-feature cache, identity and raw preprocessing hash validated through the reference protocol
interpretation: Report fold consistency and paired participant CI. No automatic best-lag selection. CIs are descriptive, unadjusted for multiplicity; overlapping training folds limit inference. High +10 is an audit signal, not a production candidate. No physiological delay or proprietary PM internal-support claim.
